title: How to Set Up Your Device
instruction_body: We’ll now set up your RestoreX device to treat your specific diagnosis. What indication are you using the RestoreX device for?

title: Setting up your RestoreX to treat Peyronie’s Disease - Checking your stretched penile length
instruction_body: The RestoreX device comes set up with the standard-length rods. These can accommodate a stretched penile length of 3.75 inches(10 cm) to 6.25 inches (16 cm). If your stretched penile length is longer than 6.25 inches (16 cm), please select the option “Install longer rods” below for instructions for removing and installing the longer rods. If your stretched penile length is not longer than 6.25 inches (16 cm), please select the “Next Step” option below.

title: Using the RestoreX to treat for Peyronie’s Disease
instruction_body:
Now that you have set up your RestoreX device to treat for your specific Peyronie’s curve, you can now being using the device.

Key Principles to Optimize Outcomes
- Only use with a flaccid penis (not erect).
- Use 30-60 minutes daily – do not skip days if possible. Separate 30 minute treatment sessions by at least 30 minutes.
- The white bands should NOT be visible during use.
- The penile skin should be loose during use – you may need to pull in additional scrotal or penile skin during use.

title: Using the RestoreX to treat for Peyronie’s Disease - Prepare your device
instruction_body: Slide the device back to the beginning location

title: Using the RestoreX to treat for Peyronie’s Disease - Prepare your device
instruction_body: Lock springs by pushing (compressing) the device together.

title: Using the RestoreX to treat for Peyronie’s Disease - Prepare your device
instruction_body: Wrap head of penis with self-adherent wrap or gauze. *Note – pull back foreskin prior to placement if present.

title: Clamp the penis on the device
instruction_body: Place the flaccid (not erect) penis through the base ring and into the clamp. *Note – rim of head of penis should be placed just inside of raised edge of clamp. Clamp should be secured as tightly as possible (without causing pain) to prevent slipping out.

title: Add Straight Traction - Extend
instruction_body: Extend the device as far out as you are able.

title: Add Straight Traction - Release
instruction_body: Release springs by pushing the device against your body. Pull in additional penile and scrotal skin as needed to ensure that penile skin is loose while receiving traction.

title: Add Straight Traction - Optimize
instruction_body: Verfiy the ammount of traction. Which describes your situation?
btn1_text: Indicator rod is not sufficiently compressed
btn2_text: Indicator rod is nearly completely compressed.

title: Add Straight Traction - Optimize
instruction_body: Lock the springs by pushing the device against your body. Advance the device 1 or more clicks until the penis is under maximal stretch. Release the springs by pushing the device against your body
btn1_text: Indicator rod is not sufficiently compressed
btn2_text: Indicator rod is nearly completely compressed.

title: Add Straight Traction - Optimize
instruction_body: Optimal traction is being delivered. Periodically check indicator rods to see if additional traction is required.

title: Straight Traction - Treatment Time
instruction_body: Continue in the straight stretch for at least 15 minutes.

title: Counterbending - Compress
instruction_body: Counterbending is only used in cases of penile curvature or indentation/hourglass deformities. Fully collapse device while keeping the penis clamped. This is done by compressing the springs and sliding the device back to the base. *Note – be very careful to avoid pinching scrotal skin as the device returns to the body.

title: Counterbending - Rotate
instruction_body: Counterbend the device by pressing the twoside blue buttons simultaneously as shown to the right. For curves in the middle or end of the penis, get to the 3rd or 4th position. For curves near the base of the body, get to the 2nd position and place a gauze roll at the base of the penis as shown on page 11. Note: for comfort, you may wish to wrap the shaft of the penis with gauze or toilet paper to allow it to slide more easily during counterbending.

title: Counterbending - Release
instruction_body: Release springs by pushing the device against your body. Pull in additional penile and scrotal skin as needed to ensure that penile skin is loose while receiving traction.

title: Counterbending - Treatment Time
instruction_body: Continue in the counterbend stretch for at least 15 minutes.

title: Removing the Device
instruction_body: Fully collapse device while keeping the penis clamped. This is done by compressing the springs and sliding the device back to the base. Press the release button to free the penis from the device. Remove any penile wraps.

title: Store the Device
instruction_body: Store the device with the springs in the uncompressed state.

title: Expected Symptoms
instruction_body:
It is normal for the head of the penis to be blue/cold while in the clamp.
- Discomfort is normal while using traction, particularly during the first 1-2 weeks of use.
- A small amount of decreased sensation is also normal during the treatment duration.
- Mild skin sensitivity from use of penile wraps is common.
- Discontinue use and contact your medical provider if you have any moderate or severe symptoms or symptoms which are persistent after discontinuing traction.

title: How to find your stretched penile length
instruction_body: Hold the tip of the penis and pull it outward from the body until maximally stretched. With a ruler, measure from the tip of the penis to the base of the penis in the flacid state. Important: The base is where the penis attaches to the pubic bone. If you have a fat pad at the base of the penis (very common), push the ruler into this pad to properly measure the full penile length.

title: Installing Longer Rods
instruction_body: To install the longer rods on your device first begin by separating the pelvic ring and extenstion rods. This can be done by pressing the extension release button on the bottom of the device and pulling on the pelvic ring. using a philips screwdriver you can unscrew the extension rods from the pelvic ring. You can then insert the longer extension rods back on the pelvic ring and screw them to the pelvic ring. You can then slide the traction device back onto the extension rods. *Note: Do not overtighten the screws.

title: Setting up your RestoreX to treat a Ventral Curve
instruction_body: The RestoreX device is designed to be adjustable for your specific curve direction. Begin by separating the pelvic ring and extenstion rods. This can be done by pressing the extension release button on the bottom of the device and pulling on the pelvic ring. using a philips screwdriver you can unscrew the extension rods from the pelvic ring. To set up your device to treat a ventral curve you should reattatch the extension rods to the top two holes in the pelvic ring. Once the rods have been attatched slide the traction device back onto the extension rods. *Note: Do not overtighten the screws.

title: Setting up your RestoreX to treat a Lateral Curve (bending towards the left)
instruction_body: The RestoreX device is designed to be adjustable for your specific curve direction. Begin by separating the pelvic ring and extenstion rods. This can be done by pressing the extension release button on the bottom of the device and pulling on the pelvic ring. using a philips screwdriver you can unscrew the extension rods from the pelvic ring. To set up your device to treat a left lateral curve you should reattatch the extension rods to the two holes in the pelvic ring on the right. Once the rods have been attatched slide the traction device back onto the extension rods. Ensure your device replicates the final graphic shown below before continuing.  *Note: Do not overtighten the screws.

title: Setting up your RestoreX - Adjusting the Clamp Position
instruction_body: To adjust the clamp position you'll need to advance the clamp housing along the clamp arms. You can do this by removing the screws that attatch the clamp housing to the clamp arms with a phillips screwdriver. You can then advance the housing to the middle hole on the clamp arms and then insert and tighten the screws. Note* Do not overtighten the screws.

title: Setting up your RestoreX - Adjusting the Clamp Position
instruction_body: To adjust the clamp position you'll need to advance the clamp housing along the clamp arms. You can do this by removing the screws that attatch the clamp housing to the clamp arms with a phillips screwdriver. You can then advance the housing to the furthest hole on the clamp arms and then insert and tighten the screws. Note* Do not overtighten the screws.

title: It is difficult to use the device due to inability to see the penis
instruction_body:
- Remove the clamp from the clamp housing (Step 3, pg. 8).
- Once removed, place the penis through the pelvic ring. With the clamp out of the housing,
secure the head of the penis in the clamp.
-Replace the clamp into its housing and continue treatment

title: Penis is too short for the device
instruction_body:
- Remove the clamp from the clamp housing.
- Counterbend the device upwards by one or two clicks.
- Place the penis through the pelvic ring. With the clamp out of the housing, secure the head
of the penis in the clamp.
- Replace the clamp into its housing and continue with treatment.
- If the penis is still unable to be clamped despite the above efforts, call PathRight Medical Customer Support for additional information.

title: Penis is too long to get a full stretch
instruction_body: Contact PathRight Medical Customer Support: Support@pathrightmedical.com

title: I need the long rods for straight stretch and short rods for counterbending
instruction_body: Contact PathRight Medical Customer Support: Support@pathrightmedical.com

title: Stretched penile length is greater than 6.25 in (15.875 cm) but with the clamp in position 2 or 3, the user cannot reach the first notch on the extension rods
instruction_body:
In a few situations, the stretched penile length obtained will indicate to use the extended rods. However, if in the process, you move the clamp to position 2 or 3, you may not be able to use the extended rods due to the extra length in the overall
device brought about by moving the clamp. If this happens, return to the standard rod and
proceed with treatment.

title: What if my penis is too short for the angled position?
instruction_body: First, use position 1 for the clamp location. Second, begin each session with 15 minutes of straight traction before bending. Third, return RestoreX to its fully collapsed position before counterbending. If, after these steps, you are still unable to bend to the recommended position, bend as far as you are able and engage the traction. If helpful, wrap the shaft of the penis with gauze (wrap only once with gauze for prewrap), or something similar to allow it to slide over the RestoreX device more easily. If after all of these steps, you are still unable to bend to the 90 degree position (position #3), bend as far as you are able and engage the traction.

title: What if my curvature is further back on the penis than the point of bending?
instruction_body: This is acceptable. In a clinical trial evaluating RestoreX, curvatures that were closer to the body responded just as well as those that were directly over the point of bending. Bending is important because it allows more force to be applied to the direction of curvature than other areas of the penis. If the distance from the penis tip to the curvature of your penis is greater than 4 in (10.16 cm), only use the first or second stop (30° or 60°). Limiting the angle of opposite force will increase the tension applied to the disease location.

title: Contraindications
instruction_body:
Do not use RestoreX if:
- You have had penile, scrotal or pelvic surgery within the past six weeks unless otherwise
indicated by your medical provider.
- You experience chronic penile pain not related to Peyronie’s disease.
- You experience chronic testicular or scrotal pain.
- You have open sores or wounds on your penis.
RestoreX is not recommended for use in men with severe vascular disease including those
who have:
- Absence of feeling in fingers, toes or limbs due to ischemia or neuropathy associated with
diabetes or similar conditions, especially if the condition has resulted in loss of digits or limbs.
- Penile skin infections, open lesions or sores.

title: Warnings and Precautions
instruction_body:
Warnings:

- Do not use the device for longer than recommended, add additional traction to the device
through the use of external materials such as weights, or overtighten the clamp as these may
potentially result in pain or damage to the penile, testicular, or scrotal anatomy/physiology.
- Do not use a soiled or dirty device as this may potentially lead to infection.
- Use caution when clamping the head of the penis, locking the tension rods, and sliding the
extension release as these may result in pinching of skin. This may potentially lead to bruising,
bleeding, irritation, skin lacerations, swelling, or reduced sensation.
- Do not place the shaft of the penis in the clamp as this may potentially result in penile scarring.

Precautions:

- Ensure that all screws are securely fastened before use of the device.
- Do not use the device if it is damaged or place it in a dishwasher or microwave oven.
- Care should be taken while placing and removing wraps on the head of the penis to prevent
skin erosion or bleeding.
- Discontinue use and consult a medical professional if you experience:
  - new or worsening pain in your scrotum, penis or abdomen.
  - new curvature or indentation.
  - persistent skin discoloration, irritation, bleeding, bruising or blistering.
  - decreased skin sensation.
  - pain with traction.
  - worsening of sexual function.

If any serious incident occurs, contact PathRight Medical and the competent authority in your location.
